articleTitle: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis: Psychological Interventions for Posttraumatic Stress Disorder in Internally Displaced and Refugee Youth.
takeaways: This systematic review identified a significant gap in evidence-based psychological interventions specifically designed for refugee and internally displaced youth with PTSD, highlighting the need for more targeted research in this vulnerable population

The study found that refugee and internally displaced children and adolescents experience disproportionately high rates of post-traumatic stress symptoms compared to general populations, emphasizing the urgent need for specialized mental health support

The meta-analysis revealed insufficient high-quality evidence to definitively recommend specific psychological intervention approaches for this population, indicating current treatment protocols may not be adequately validated for refugee youth

The research demonstrates that standard PTSD interventions developed for general populations may require significant adaptation or replacement with culturally-sensitive approaches when treating displaced youth populations
